All the model elements are directly derived from hot S-parameters, rather than cold S-parameters, by using vector fitting (VF) method The model renders excellent agreement with the measured and simulated data over 1 to 100 GHz, for a 2×150μm GaAs HEMT device manufactured in CETC-55 150nm GaAs pHEMT technology.

articleTitle: An 18 to 40GHz double balanced MMIC mixer using GaAs technology
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper describes a broadband, doubled balanced diode ring mixer IC. The RF/LO frequency range is 18 to 40 GHz and the IF DC to 8 GHz. This chip is fabricated on the 0.15μm pHEMT GaAs process which is offered by WIN semiconductor. The modified Marchand balun is used to provide the differential signals for the mixer. The chip successfully get a conversion loss less than 12dB and decent LO to IF isolation of nearly over 20dB. The mixer's size is around 1.10mm×0.75mm.

articleTitle: Dual-resonant terahertz metamaterial with high Q-factors
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A dual-resonant THz metamaterial with high Q-factor property is proposed in this letter. Two semi-circle resonator with rectangular substrate are chosen as unit cell of the metamaterial. Numerical simulations reveal that the metamaterial can perform strong absorption peak of more than 90% and high Q-factor more than 30 simultaneously. Moreover, the dipole-dipole interaction model is used to analysis the operating principle of the proposed structure. The metamaterial has such advantages of simple structure, strong absorption and high Q-factor. In the future, it may be employed as high-performance sensors or filters.

articleTitle: A design of wide IF bandwidth GaAs passive mixer with new balun structure
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper reports a 0.15um GaAs MMIC double balanced mixer with working frequency 7-14GHz for wideband applications. The proposed mixer applies a new type of Marchand balun structure to simplify the impedance matching. The comparison with tradition one shows that it also helps to diminish the chip area. For the output port of mixer, the isolation between RF and IF is also taken into account in this design by building a low pass filter for IF signal. The on-wafer measurement of this mixer shows that the minimum conversion loss is less than 7dB. The bandwidth of IF can cover the whole bandwidth between 1MHz-6.5GHz with the ripple less than 1.3dB. The circuit also exhibits excellent return loss at LO and RF ports. The chip area is 1130um×850 um.

articleTitle: Compact tri-band bandpass filter with controllable frequency using stub-loaded triple-mode resonator
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A novel microstrip tri-band bandpass filter with controllable center frequencies by applying stub-loaded triple-mode resonator is presented. The resonator is constructed by loading a stepped-impedance stub (SIS) and an open stub on a traditional stepped-impedance resonator (SIR). The novel resonator can be utilized to design tri-band BPF. In addition, four transmission zeros generated by the resonator can improve the passband selectivity greatly. Center frequency and bandwidth of the tri-band BPF can be easily adjusted by tuning the stub length and coupling gaps respectively. To verify the application feasibility, a compact planar tri-band BPF is simulated, fabricated and measured. The simulated and measured results are in good agreement and show excellent in-band performance and sharp selectivity.

articleTitle: Device-free localization with outlier intersection rejection
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Device-free localization (DFL) is an emerging wireless technique for estimating the location of target without electronic equipment, usually by detecting the changes of the received signal strength (RSS) measurements of the wireless links. Due to the uncertaintiy of the wireless channel, wireless signal may be polluted seriously and result in error-detection. In this paper, we propose a novel intersection of link approach with outlier intersection rejection (ILOIR) for DFL. It consists of two key strategies, including: affected link identification by differential RSS detection, and target location estimation from link intersections with outlier intersection rejection. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach is robust to the fluctuation of the wireless signals with superior localization accuracy compared with the existing Radio Tomographic Imaging (RTI) approach.

articleTitle: Miniaturization design of dual-slot corrugated horn antenna on Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Combining axial slots with straight slots, a novel corrugated horn antenna on Ka-band is designed. Based on this structure, the size of the antenna can be miniaturized by reducing the number of axial slots and straight slots. The newly designed antenna is tested in HFSS. The simulations show that the an-tenna not only has good radiation characteristic and Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) performance, but also optimizes the size and the structure of the antenna.

articleTitle: Software design and implementation of WSN access gateway based on ISA100.11a
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: According to ISA100.11a standard, a new gateway access method based on application layer was proposed in this paper which realized the communication between wireless sensor networks and Ethernet. It was C/S structure and completed on the Linux operating development platform. The system mainly contained four modules: Ethernet interface module, data storage module, protocol conversion module and wireless interface module. Each module was responsible for different functions, so as to communicate and exchange data with each other for various protocols. Two test programs were carried out; experiment results showed the gateway was stable and reliable. It can effectively achieve internal data management and remote monitoring in wireless sensor networks.

articleTitle: Sub-wavelength UWB antenna array with fractal slots and split ring resonators for time reversal super-resolution focusing
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Time reversal (TR) is a useful method that can focus electromagnetic waves precisely at the desired point in both time and space. In this paper, we find that properly designed and distributed micro-scatterers in the near-field zone of antenna array contribute to overcoming the diffraction limit. By directly integrating micro-structured fractal slots (FS) and split ring resonators (SRR) into each antenna element, a novel and linear array of CPW-fed UWB antennas is proposed to focus TR waves with a spatial super-resolution, in which the spacing between adjacent elements is 1/12 wavelength. With small dimensions of 29*43*32 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and wide impedance bandwidth of 2.35GHz-11.5GHz, this proposed array is attractive for TR-UWB-MIMO communication applications.

articleTitle: A compact band-pass filter using transformed radial stubs with ultra-wide stopband
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A compact microstrip band-pass filter (BPF) with ultra-wide-band rejection and compact size by using transformed radial stubs (TRS) is presented. Three TRS cells and two shunt stubs are used in the design. The implemented 2.5 GHz BPF with a bandwidth of 19% using three TRS cells demonstrates more than 22-dB rejection from 3 to 23 GHz (up to 9.2f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>). The measured passband insertion loss is 2.15dB and the board size of the BPF is only 0.251 × 0.211λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>, without using any lumped elements.

articleTitle: A dual-polarized patch antenna with pattern reconfigurable characteristics
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper presents a dual linearly-polarized patch antenna with pattern reconfigurable characteristics. The antenna can achieve ±45° dual-polarization with three modes. By changing the states of switches, the maximum radiation direction points to +25°, -2° and -26° in the elevation angle (x-z plane), with 3dB beamwidth covering the range from -48° to +44°. The three modes have a common band of 2.11-2.57GHz, with relative bandwidth of 18.77%. Simulation results show that good impedance matching, stable gain and high front-to-back ratio are achieved simultaneously. The antenna can be used in wireless communications systems.

articleTitle: Progress and opportunities in InP HBT terahertz monolithic integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: The terahertz wave is a very significant cross-frontier field. While the rapid progress on characteristic frequency of over-600GHz InP-based integrated circuit technology, it provides process foundation for solid-state terahertz circuits and system with high performance and high integration. The overview is made on the research progress of solid-state terahertz amplifiers, and the device modeling and de-embedding technique are also discussed. Finally, the progress and trend of terahertz monolithic integrated circuit (TMIC) technology in China is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A broadband, low power, variable-gain power amplifier based on 0.13-µm CMOS technology
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A 6.336-6.864GHz power amplifier for band 7 of ultra-wideband(UWB) is presented in this paper, which consists of a differential cascode output stage and a gain-tuning stage by changing bias voltage. Implemented in 0.13-μm CMOS technology, the power amplifier has a gain range of -14-1dB, output 1-dB compression point of +1dBm and output third order intercept point(OIP3) of +11dBm. Simulation results also show that the output return loss (S22) is -17dB and the isolation (S12) is -45 dB at input frequency of 6.6 GHz. The power amplifier has a low power consumption of only 16.8mW from 1.2V supply voltage. The die area is 0.68×0.68 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Modeling of LTCC microstrip to stripline vertical via transition exploiting space mapping technique
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper presents a method for modeling LTCC microstrip to stripline vertical via transition taking advantage of the space mapping technique. ADS is utilized to construct the coarse model. The value of equivalent circuit elements are expressed by quadratic functions due to the three points in one degree of the base set. In this paper, a flexible mapping is exploited in the method for considering the trade off between time and accuracy in the extraction process. The proposed model shows a good performance in approximation and prediction from the comparison with fine model response and surrogate model response.

articleTitle: Design of RF receiver front-end with bandpass and hairpin resonator narrow band filter for high speed intelligent DSRC application
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, RF receiver front-end applying high speed intelligent DSRC (Dedicated Short Range Communication) systems is presented. The proposed chip includes a current-reused LNA, a folded Giber cell mixer, a Colpitts VCO, and SIR pseudo-inter digital bandpass filter. This design of the 5.8GHz band filter design using micro strip structures like pseudo-inter digital cavity to form band-pass filters, impedance matching to enhance this through a different filter device's performance. Band pass filter center frequency at 5.8 GHz, insertion loss of 2.5dB, band-pass of the return loss is about 20 dB. A cross-coupled planar microwave elliptic function filter using coupled microstrip miniaturized hairpin resonators at the frequency 5.8 GHz band is designed and implemented. To construct band pass filter, parallel and series resonance characteristics of electrical, magnetic or mixed coupling are discussed. Theoretical analysis is used to illustrate the different coupling functions. The designed hairpin resonator narrow band pass filter achieves a measured bandwidth of 30 MHz, an insertion loss less than 1.4 dB and return loss higher than 30 dB. The measured results show an input return loss of 20 dB, a conversion gain of 29 dB, a double-side band (DSB) noise figure (NF) of 5 dB, and a third-order intercept point (IIP3) of −24.4 dBm. The on-chip oscillator shows the measured tuning range of 5.17–5.98 GHz and phase noise of −118.5 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset from the 5.8 GHz carrier with a power consumption of 27.6 mW from a 1 V supply voltage.

articleTitle: Microwave metamaterial absorber with nλ0/2 dielectric thicknesses
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Most of the metamaterial absorbers are thin planar configurations, of which the thicknesses of dielectric slabs are much smaller than 1/10 of the absorbing wavelength. On increasing the thicknesses of dielectric slabs in limited scales, the absorptions become poor. And the surface currents in metal resonators and ground planes are anti-parallel. In this paper, we theoretically demonstrate that, when thicken the dielectric slab of a conventional metamaterial absorber for nλ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>/2 (n=1, 2, …), it can also achieve the near-unit absorption properties and the surface currents in metal resonator and ground plane are not associated any longer. Moreover, the electromagnetic wave energy can be completely absorbed by the metal resonators and the main function of ground plane is to reflect the incident EM waves back to the metal resonators. These findings can broaden the potential applications of the metamaterial absorbers in microwave and optics areas, especially in the invisible screens for large area objectives.

articleTitle: A new method of designing high efficiency and wideband power amplifier
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper presents a new method to design high efficiency and wideband power amplifier (PA). Based on the output parasitics network of MOSFET, this method shifts the optimum load impedances from the intrinsic plane to the package plane, which are obtained by the continuous PA theory and then rectified elaborately by multi-harmonic bilateral-pull technology, in order to make the second harmonic load impedances in high efficient region as well as the fundamental load impedances with high power added efficiency (PAE) and output power. A simulated example based on the GaN HEMT device CGH40010F is designed to verify the proposed method.

articleTitle: Stable analysis of Fast Independent Vector Analysis algorithm
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: The Fast Independent Vector Analysis (FastIVA) algorithm [1] is an effective approach to achieve the joint blind source separation (JBSS) problem. However, the authors in [1] do not give the stable analysis for the FastIVA algorithm. In this paper, we extend the work of Intae Lee et al [1] by deriving conditions for local stability for the more general case of noncircular sources. Simulations demonstrate the correctness of our stability analysis.

articleTitle: Design of frequency synthesizer based on multiple VCO
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper introduces a design of frequency synthesizer based on the combination of multi VCO. The combination of multiple VCO can output a wide frequency range of the signal, VCO signal after the decimal frequency divider, and reference signal phase, control VCO error signal obtained, locked. A combination of multiple VCO can improve the phase noise of the output signals, but will bring the loop bandwidth is not consistent, power and other aspects of the problem, through the control of the VCO power supply and variable bandwidth loop filter design, a good solution to the problem. The frequency synthesizer has been successfully applied to portable spectrum analyzer.

articleTitle: TDOA/DGPS hybrid location algorithm based on the initial estimation
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper makes improvements aiming at the existing problems of hybrid location algorithm combining BS and satellites data and propose the TDOA/DGPS hybrid location algorithm based on the initial estimation. According to simulations with MATLAB, this new algorithm is proved to improve positioning accuracy further and reduce the amount of computation. But this algorithm can not eliminate effect of NLOS error completely.

articleTitle: Gait pattern-aware displacement estimation in micro-sensor motion capture
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Micro-sensor motion capture (MMocap) systems do not have external references. It is challenging to estimate the displacement of human CoM (Center of Mass). This is especially true when gait pattern changes. This paper presents a novel gait pattern-aware algorithm that aims to estimate the displacement of human CoM during walking and jumping for MMocap systems. Firstly, we fuse the acceleration of sensors and hierarchical information of the body to detect the gait patterns. Secondly, according to the detected patterns, the displacement is adaptively calculated. 1) During walking the displacement is calculated by the extension and flexion angles of the lower body joints. 2) During jumping the displacement is calculated by integrating the acceleration of the root joint. The experimental results have demonstrated that our algorithm estimates the displacements accurately during both walking and jumping.

articleTitle: InP DHBT submillimeter-wave modeling based on electromagnetic simulation method
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, a novel large-signal InP DHBT model upto Submillimeter-wave frequencies is proposed. The intrinsic part of HBT based on the improved agilentHBT model and EM simulation technique is presented to account for the distributed effect of interconnection of the fingers and their surroundings. The combined model implemented in Agilent-ADS is verified by comparing the simulated and measured data in dc and multi bias S-parameters. Good agreement between the measured and the simulated result has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Wireless indoor positioning based on filtering algorithm
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: The paper proposed filtering algorithms for wireless indoor localization based on Extended Kalman filtering (EKF) and Uncented Kalman filtering (UKF). When we use EKF linearization to deal with nonlinear problems, it may cause precision decrease and a series of problems. Thus, the rigorous mathematical analysis simulations and comparative results were carried out in this paper to compare EKF and UKF for the wireless indoor localization. Finally, the advantages and disadvantages of two algorithms and their respective applications were obtained. The simulation results show that the algorithm accuracy of UKF is higher than that of EKF, especially in the nonlinear environment.

articleTitle: Fast optimization method of polarization receiving power for monostatic condition based on Kennaugh matrix
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Different polarization incidences and/or inflections yield different polarization scattering powers. The problem of searching optimal polarization state for the maximal polarization receiving power (PRP) is of significantly meaningful. Usually, there are no analytic solutions to the problem and current numerical methods are time consuming. Aiming to reduce the computational time, fast optimization mechanism is studied in this paper. An improved Lagrange method (ILM) based on bisection strategy is proposed for monostatic condition. This method takes the advantage of monotonicity of a cost function constructed by Lagrange multiplier to accelerate searching speed. The performance of this method is validated by comparing with the Lagrange method proposed by Chen (LMC). Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method in this paper is superior to the existing method.

articleTitle: Recognition and localization of boundary and isolated nodes in wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: There are boundary nodes and a certain number of the isolated nodes in the wireless sensor network. If conducting the effective judgment and processing over them, the positioning errors of the entire network will be reduced. Based on principles and approaches of the graphic theory, the boundary nodes and isolated nodes will be judged. Through an analysis on the node density and the range and direction of the receiving anchor nodes, the judgment and positioning approaches for the boundary nodes and the isolated nodes in the wireless sensor network can then be come up with. The simulation experiment for positioning performance in different situation suggested that the positioning accuracy of the misbehavior nodes will be improved by over 17% after the modification while the one of the isolated nodes in the irregular network topology after modification will be improved by over 10%.

articleTitle: Substrate integrated nonradiative dielectric waveguide bandpass filter
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper presented a novel substrate integrated nonradiative dielectric (SINRD) waveguide bandpass filter based on Print Circuit Boards (PCBs). Firstly, by drilling an array of square via-slot or circular via-slot patterns in a substrate we can realize a waveguiding dielectric channel similar to the canonical nonradiative dielectric (NRD) waveguide. Choosing the geometry of the via-slot patterns carefully could minimized the leakage loss which come from the uncovered part. Then, by applying the same principle of alternating-width type of NRD waveguide bandpass filter, we realized a SINRD waveguide bandpass filter in an advanced 3D electromagnetic field simulator. Simulation results demonstrated that the PCB version of SINRD waveguide filter is a promising component for the millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: Design of planar narrow band millimetre-wave filter with wide stop-band
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper presents a planar millimetre-wave (mmwave) band pass filter based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) and substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL) techniques. Four half wavelength mircrostrip resonators are imbedded in the SIW cavity to improve Q-factor. Due to the closed configuration which eliminates radiation loss, the filter presents a relatively low insertion loss. The proposed filter has a 3dB fractional bandwidth of 1.6% across frequencies from 29.8GHz to 30.3 GHz and 20dB rejection band from 30.7GHz to 58 GHz.

articleTitle: Asymptotically Optimized Subspace Pursuit for sparse signal recovery
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A novel greedy algorithm, termed the Asymptotically Optimized Subspace Pursuit (AOSP), is proposed in this paper for recovery of sparse signals. In the Subspace Pursuit (SP) algorithm, the measurement vector is projected onto the optimal subspace and the original sparse signals are recovered on the basis of the projection coefficients. However, the SP algorithm uses the sparsity K as a priori to determine the dimension of the optimal subspace, which makes it difficult to be applied in real applications. To avoid this deficiency, we use a statistical method to progressively estimate the dimension of the optimal subspace. Therefore, the priori signal sparsity isn't needed any more and the proposed AOSP can be adaptive to any natural signals. Numerical experiments are implemented for sparse signal models when the measurement is perturbed by the Gaussian white noise. The simulation results show that the proposed AOSP can achieve the higher recovery accuracy compared to other several typical greedy algorithms. Finally, the experiment of compressed sensing for image recovery is implemented, and the simulation results show that among several candidate greedy algorithms the proposed AOSP can achieve the best image quality.

articleTitle: Tunable diode-based predistortion linearizer for power amplifier with a phase expansion or compression at millimeter-wave frequency
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: We propose an analog predistortion linearizer based on diode at millimeter-wave frequency. Taking advantage of tuning the bias of the diodes, the linearizer is capable of providing different combinations of the amplitude and phase characteristics for the use of solid-state power amplifier (SSPA) and travelling wave tube amplifier (TWTA). The experiment validation shows that, about 6.1 dB gain expansion and 20 ° phase compression can be compensated for SSPA and about 3.4 dB gain expansion and 12 ° phase expansion can be obtained for use with TWTA at millimeter-wave frequency.

articleTitle: Research on the basic education resources sharing model based on cloud computing
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In recent years, the research on the resources sharing has made great progress in education area. But it is far from reaching the needs of teachers and students because of the great investment, poor management and service, low intelligence and poor scalability of present Basic Education Resources Sharing Model. With full use of the advantages of cloud computing, such as super computing ability, high reliability, high scalability, on-demand service, low cost, this paper intends to adopt cloud computing technology to design the model of basic education resources sharing platform and expatiate it's realization mechanism. The platform will offer a new solution for Basic Education Resources Sharing, which can save human, material and financial resources on repetition development and provide more high quality learning resources and references for teachers and students. The platform will also promote the integration of information technology with curricula and improve the imbalanced education development and gradually elevate the overall quality of education.

articleTitle: Sparse representation based method for off-grid frequency estimation
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This work investigates the problem of estimating the K frequency components of a mixture of complex sinusoids. Component frequencies of practical signals are not assumed to lie on a specified grid, but any values in the normalized frequency domain (0, 1). To estimate the off-grid frequencies, we apply the first Taylor expansion to approximate the true unknown dictionary and establish a more accurate model for sparse approximation of practical complex sinusoids. Furthermore, we reformulate this model and develop a fast method alternating between a sparse recovery problem solved using the multi-measurement vector orthogonal matching pursuit (MOMP) algorithm and a least squares (LS) problem to speed up the estimating process. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve off-grid frequency estimation of complex sinusoids with low computational cost as well as high estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: The non-polynomial function to detect outliers in independent component analysis
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: The separation performance of fast independent component analysis (ICA) can be damaged by outliers. However, the traditional model only discusses the condition that ICA is free of outliers. In general, those measurements that significantly deviate from the normal pattern of sensed data are considered as outliers. In the observed signals of ICA, outliers include noise and errors. Whereas, the traditional techniques used to find the outliers can not be used in ICA directly due to the constraint of the independence of the sources signals. In this paper, a non-polynomial function-based method is proposed to detect the outliers in the signals of ICA. Simulations show the effectiveness of the proposed approach to find the outliers in the observed data.

articleTitle: Two UWB-MIMO antennas with high isolation using isolation stubs
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, two Ultra-wideband (UWB) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antennas with different isolation structures are proposed. A comb U stub and an inverted-T stub are designed to improve the isolation between two antenna elements. Over the whole ultra-wide bandwidth, the return losses are better than 10 dB, and the isolation between two elements are better than 20 dB. The simulation and measurement results agree with each other very well. The proposed antennas are suitable for some portable UWB MIMO/diversity applications.

articleTitle: Compressive sampling for DS TT&C signals based on sparsity analysis
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Broadband is one of development trends of the TT&C system, which will inevitably lead to high speed sampling pressure and massive data problem. To aim at the issue, the compressive sampling for DS TT&C signals based on compressive sensing was studied preliminarily. On the basis of the in-depth sparse analysis for the DS TT&C signal, the phase-Doppler basic dictionary was built, and then simulation verification of the sparse representation and compressive sampling for the DS TT&C signal was carry out. The results of simulation show that compressive sampling for DS TT&C signals based on the built phase-Doppler basic dictionary is feasible which gets some noise reduction performance.

articleTitle: Dual-band antenna based on epsilon-negative transmission line for body-centric communication
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band low-profile antenna based on the epsilon negative (ENG) meta-structured transmission line (MTL) for wireless body centric communications is presented. It is composed of four unit-cells with modified mushroom-like structures. The physical size and operational frequencies of the antenna are both determined by the epsilon negative unit-cell. More importantly, besides low profile and simplicity of the antenna configuration, its admirable radiation characteristics, i. e., Omni-directional pattern in azimuth plane at low frequency band (for on-body communication) and Uni-directional pattern in elevation plane at upper frequency band (for off-body communication), could be well obtained, which is quite suitable for body-centric communication applications.

articleTitle: A F-band balanced power amplifier in 0.15µm GaAs pHEMT process
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: The design of balanced power amplifier (PA) is proposed in this manuscript which is operated from 46.0 to 66.5 GHz. The circuit is fabricated in WIN 0.15 µm GaAs pHEMT process. The performance of circuit is designed for achieving high output power and broadband characteristics. To further reduce the layout area for the coupler design, the three-dimensional of vertical coupling mode was used in the PA circuit. The circuit exhibits the small-signal gain of 10.0 dB. The maximum output power is up to 10 dBm. The total chip area including on-chip coupler is 1.16 × 0.79 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: An optimization model of the stripline-to-stripline vertical interconnect in LTCC technology
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper presents a microwave stripline-to-stripline vertical interconnect in Low Temperature Co-fired Ceramic (LTCC) Technology. Two circular grooves are separately designed in the stripline lower ground plane and the stripline upper ground plane to reduce the insertion loss and improve the return loss. The mentioned structure has been simulated by HFSS. According to the simulation comparison results, the insertion loss can reduce 0.04 dB on average and the return loss can increase 17.5 dB on average over a band from 0.3 Ghz to 30 Ghz.

articleTitle: Low phase noise LC VCO with self-bias tail
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper presents a low phase noise LC VCO. The VCO adopts a switched current topology. Theoretical analysis is given to show how phase noise is optimized. The reduction of current tail's 1/f noise and the elimination of fixed current bias voltage are the two main contributions to phase noise reduction. A 1.8-2.25 GHz VCO is implemented and measured for the proposed circuits, achieving phase noise at 1-MHz offset from a 2.01-GHz carrier of -125 dBc/Hz with a 2-V supply.

articleTitle: The design of multi-frequency combiner based on common cavity
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper introduces a design method of multi-frequency combiner based on common cavity. It comes from the dualband filter structure with a common cavity, which is based on the General Chebyshev filter. The key to this method is to get the normalized capacitance c0 of the common cavity and coupling coefficients of the multi-frequency combiner. And writing a matlab program can make it easier to get the parameters we need. Using a common cavity to realize multi-frequency combiner cannot only reduce the amount of taps, but also can make the intermodulation better. In order to verify the method described, a multi-frequency combiner is introduced, whose test result is in conformity with the simulation results, which verifies the correctness and superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Investigating antenna phase pattern by electromagnetic simulation software
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: According to one definition, antenna phase center is the center of sphere on which the phase of the radiated field has the minimum change over certain elevation angle (θ) and azimuth angle (Φ) ranges. In case when the phase center of the radiated field is needed to be considered, the commercial electromagnetic simulation software can be utilized to obtain the phase pattern so as to find out the phase variation of the radiated field over the interested angular range. This paper will compare the simulated phase pattern obtained from different simulation software with the calculated result and will discuss the relationship between antenna phase pattern and phase center by modeling a simple patch antenna in the simulation software.

articleTitle: High-power first-order Gaussian pulse-fed bow-tie time-domain antenna
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A method of using the center frequency of the fed signal spectrum -10dB bandwidth to design high-power bow-tie time-domain antenna is mentioned. This antenna fed signal is first-order Gaussian pulse. Blumlein formative line specially designed plays a first-order differential role in the process of changing Gaussian pulse produced by Photoconductive semiconductor switches (PCSS) into a first-order Gaussian pulse. Antenna and blumlein formative line model-building and simulation are established by the antenna theory and CST2009 basing on the method of FDTD. The technical parameters of the antenna (such as S11, Fidelity, Time-domain pattern etc.) are optimized so that the antenna has a very wide bandwidth, good fidelity, wide time-domain pattern, stable phase center and high power.

articleTitle: An optimization approach to cell association and resource allocation in heterogeneous cellular networks
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In heterogeneous cellular networks (HCNs), it is highly desirable to design a cell association strategy that can actively offload mobile users to less congested small cells. Such a cell association strategy needs to be considered in conjunction with resource allocation. In this paper we take an optimization approach to analyze joint cell association and resource allocation in a two tier HCN. We formulize a utility maximization problem with the square root function as the utility function, and with proper relaxation of constraints, we are able to solve this problem and obtain an optimal solution that improves network throughput. Numerical results show that our approach achieves load balancing across macro and small cell BSs, and provide higher network throughput compared to the max SINR and max log sum association schemes. Our results also show that the optimal solution takes a tradeoff between user fairness and network throughput.

articleTitle: Design of A Ka-band mode converter with rectangular waveguide TE10 mode to a coaxial waveguide TM01 mode
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A novel mode converter is introduced in this paper, transferring the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode, which is the dominant mode in rectangular waveguide into TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode in coaxial waveguide. The simulation and optimization is based on CST and good results have been achieved with the VSWR 1.2 at 34.5GHz center frequency and the efficiency is greater than 86%. The test results agree well with the simulation, certifying the feasibility of the structure.

articleTitle: Cascaded trisection linear-phase filter
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper presents a new method to design Cascaded trisection(CT) linear-phase filters. In order to verify this method, we designed a band-pass HTS filter by using resonator deformation and improvement to achieve the CT structure and introducing a group delay equalizer to equalize group delay within the pass-band. Eventually we achieve an eight-order HTS filter with center frequency 899.5 MHz, bandwidth 19 MHz, band insertion loss better than 0.2 dB, band rejection better than 50 dB within 0.6 MHz at higher stop-band, group delay fluctuation better than 1.5 ns within 50% of the pass-band. All these parameters would meet the requirement of linear phase filter.

articleTitle: An improved-performance decoding algorithm of LDPC codes for layered decoding
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In order to reduce the bit error rate of low-density parity-check codes for layered decoding algorithm and improve the decoding convergence speed, an improved layered decoding algorithm is proposed. In layered decoding algorithm, updated bit nodes information can be used by check nodes in the iteration process while in dynamic decoding algorithm check nodes update in order according to the reliability. The proposed algorithm combines advantages of the layered and dynamic decoding algorithm. Moreover, compared with the definition of remaining information for check nodes in the dynamic decoding algorithm, a new method to evaluate the reliability is defined in the proposed algorithm. Based on 1/2 code rate china mobile multimedia broadcasting standard, simulation and comparison between the conventional layered decoding algorithm and the proposed layered decoding algorithm have been carried out. The simulation results show that under the same bit error rate, the signal to noise ratio of the improved algorithm reduces nearly 0.4dB as well as convergence speed improves obviously. The proposed layered decoding algorithm reduces the bit error rate and improves the reliability of data in communication system which uses LDPC codes as the channel coding.

articleTitle: UWB waveguide bandpass filter with two ultra narrow notched bands
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A compact ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass filter (BPF) with two notched bands based on ridged waveguide is presented. Capacitive loading short stub structures are introduced to reject the undesired wireless local-area network (WLAN) radio signals (i.e., 5.2-and-5.8-GHz bands). By independently adjusting the heights of the capacitive loading posts in the short stubs, the centre frequencies of two notched bands can be allocated at 5.2 and 5.8 GHz, while the bandpass is almost not affected. A UWB BPF has been simulated, fabricated and measured, with good agreement between the simulated and measured results. Good passband and stopband performances are achieved. Specifically, the two notched bands centered at 5.2 and 5.8 GHz have 10 dB rejection fractional bandwidths of about 2.3% and 2.06%, respectively.

articleTitle: Frequency reconfigurable antenna for cognitive radio applications
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A new antenna suitable for cognitive radio system is proposed. The structure of the antenna is composed of an ultra wide band (UWB) sensing antenna, and a frequency reconfigurable communicating antenna. It has a capability to operate in wide band (2.4-12GHz) and three narrow bands (band I: 3.05-3.8GHz, band II: 2.35-2.98 GHz, 4.3-4.5GHz and band III: 1.45-2.18GHz). Three switches are used to control the antenna working at different narrow band.

articleTitle: An optimized filter design based on stepped impendence resonators
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper puts forward an optimized stepped impedance resonator (SIR)-based filter design which is able to optimize the frequency selectivity of the filters by means of an improved filter feeding method. This paper provides a filter design based on SIR. With this design, the zero-degree feeding structure can be achieved through the adjustment of the positions to tap feed lines. The frequency selectivity of the filters is thus improved. Thanks to the small size and simple construction, this type of filter can be widely applied in wireless communication fields.

articleTitle: Research on application of compressed sensing based on signal decomposition
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Based on compressed sensing (CS) theory and its classical OMP reconstruction algorithm, as to the problems that large storage of measurement matrix is needed when sampling and calculating the whole signal which has a large amount of data and that a huge amount of time is consumed when reconstructing it, we can decompose the signal into many sub-signals through a certain way, and then measure and reconstruct the sub-signals. Finally, we can realize the processing of the whole segment signal. As above, the application of compressed sensing which based on signal decomposition can be called decomposed compressed sensing method in this paper. Currently, a commonly used decomposed compressed sensing method is segmented compressed sensing (SCS). For the problem that there are errors in processing certain types of sparse signals by SCS method, we propose a new decomposed compressed sensing in this paper. The simulation results show that, compared with SCS, the new method can improve the reconstruction efficiency to a certain extent. At the same time, this method is applicable to any type of signal, which has wider application range.

articleTitle: Radiation of luneburg lens antenna in low frequency range
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A modified application of luneburg lens has been demonstrated which is used in ns-pulse radiation. Such a situation has been simulated to have a remarkable enhancement in time-domain gain, radiation pattern and received signal peak-to-peak value. Despite of diffraction of electromagnetic wave, both TEM horn antenna and vivaldi antenna have been worked well focused by the lens. Besides, an modified lunelurg lens has been designed to obtain much more convenience.

articleTitle: The research about dipole array's microwave-absorbing characteristics
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Both the back and forward transient scattering mechanisms of dipole array with different loading forms have been investigated from time-domain and frequency-domain. Using 4×8 dipole array as an example, the data of scattering from the array under the incidence of Gaussian pulses are obtained by finite differential time-domain method. The influences of the incident angle on the waveforms and loading form are analyzed and conclusions are drawn. From these characteristics and conclusions, it is possible to find a method to reduce both the back and forward scattering field of the array structure.

articleTitle: An assessment of single-particle effect in SRAM-based combinatorial coding
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In the space radiation environment, there are various cosmic rays and high-energy particles, which causing memory soft errors in memories. This is the single-particle flip effect, which is an important factor. It reduces the reliability of data transmission. In the radiation hardened design, the use of error correcting codes for reinforcement is an effective way to mitigate the single particle effect. In this paper, we analyze the bit error rate (BER) of the space and two major codings -Hamming code and BCH code. These two codings are employed to harden Static RAMs (SRAMs). These two codings' space stability and resource consumption in specific spatial conditions is studied. These analysis results can be used to select an appropriate coding for SRAM reinforcement, and choose an appropriate SRAM refresh time in different space environment.

articleTitle: Moving target detection with frequency diversity under multipath scenario
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper considers the problem of coherent integration under multipath scenario. With the geometry feature for sea multipath, the signal to noise ratio (SNR) in the receiver shows obvious fluctuation on the range-elevation dimensions plane because of varying interference effect between direct and indirect echoes. With the frequency diversity technique, a new structure detector is introduced for coherent integration. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed detector structure.

articleTitle: A rigorous process in designing quadrature hybrid
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A typical 3GHz narrow-band quadrature hybrid coupler has been proposed and measured through rigorous steps. S matrix guides the design in distributed parameter model, which further lead to a microstrip model in Advanced Design System with consideration of loss. Both HFSS and CST are referred in to further optimize the detailed parameters. The measurement shows a well matching with simulation, while errors have been figured out and confirmed. A modified ground plane has been designed with a SRR structure, to fix the frequency shift in S31. Such a consideration may transit centre frequency of S31 into middle, which less loss is referred in.

articleTitle: An efficient model for the on-chip CPWs in GaAs technology
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: An efficient and accurate model accounting for the skin and proximity effect is proposed in this paper, and a novel parameter extraction method, based on empirical formulas and measured data, is given subsequently. Several standard coplanar waveguides (CPWs) of different lengths are fabricated in GaAs technology. The per-unit-length (p.u.l.) L, C and S-parameters are compared. Up to 67GHz, the proposed model is in better agreement with the measured data than the simulated results.

articleTitle: A novel technique for defending hardware Trojan circuit
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Hardware security to ensure trust in IC has emerged as important research topic in recent years, several Trojan detection approaches have been developed to prevent the damages caused by Trojans, making Trojan insertion more and more difficult. This paper design Trojans use a novel technique, which can avoid activate Hardware Trojan in testing time. The simulation results on s38584 benchmark demonstrate that, with a negligible area overhead and power consume, our proposed method can significantly reduce the probability of Trojan detection.

articleTitle: Universal UHF RFID reader antenna based on the ferrimagnetic slab with tunable operating frequency
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A circularly polarized (CP) patch antenna based on ferrimagnetic substrate is discussed in this paper, for universal ultra-high-frequency (UHF) RF identification (RFID) applications in the Internet of Things (IOT). Such antenna is composed of top dielectric layer printed with rectangular radiation patch, middle ferrimagnetic layer, and bottom dielectric layer printed with ground plane. The ferrimagnetic layer under an applied dc magnetic bias provides the CP radiation characteristic, and most importantly, tunes arbitrarily the operating frequency band in a wide range covering all the worldwide operating frequency bands of UHF RFID, by adjusting the magnetic bias. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed antenna, under conditions of different dc magnetic biases ranged from 330 to 700 Oe, can be arbitrarily operated from 840 to 960 MHz with a narrow impedance bandwidth of about 7 MHz, a tunable gain level ranged from -1.9 to 2.5 dBic, and a wide 3-dB AR beamwidth of 120° over the impedance bandwidth.

articleTitle: Slot allocation based on virtual competition in millimeter wave
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Due to many advantages, the emerging millimeter-wave communication technology is promising in scenes like library and meeting room. The international millimeter wave standard has been completed recently while China is making its own millimeter wave standard. As the devices which work at millimeter wave frequencies can operate at overlap bandwidths, it faces the difficulties of fairness and net congestion in its media access control layer (MAC). This paper proposes a method based on virtual competition MAC resource allocation scheme. Simulation results prove that the proposed scheme could improve the compatibility of international standard and solve the congestion problem and the fairness of resource allocation with coexisted multi-mode devices.

articleTitle: Chip design of low-power phase-locked loop for FMCW MMW radar and sensor application
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A 24 GHz phase-locked loop (PLL) with a LC-tank voltage-controlled oscillates (VCO) is implemented in TSMC 90 nm CMOS for FMCW MMW radar and sensor application In this proposed circuit including a cross-coupled Colpitts VCO is adopted to decrease the transistor parasitic capacitance and reduce the phase noise. Second, an injection locked frequency divider (ILFD) is utilized in first divider stage to handle the high frequency signal. Measured results achieve that at supply voltage of 1.2 V, the VCO output frequency is tunable and the synthesizer phase noise is about −97.47 dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset from the carrier frequency. The mixed output power spectrum is −2.97 dBm at 10.2 GHz and the power consumption is 9.24 mW.

articleTitle: Generation of double-Brillouin-frequency spaced multiwavelength and millimeter wave carrier in one loop structure
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, a unique and simple one loop structure that can produce double-Brillouin-frequency spaced multiwavelength is proposed and it is used to generate millimeter waves as carriers to carry 3.2GHz signal. The double-Brillouin-frequency spaced multiwavelength one loop structure utilizes the reflection properties of fiber loop mirror composed of a 50/50 coupler and isolator to get only even Stokes wave. The space between Stokes waves about 0.1475 nm and 0.1734 nm in two different type structures, 20 GHz and 40 GHz generated millimeter wave as carrier, and demodulated 3.2 GHz signal are experimentally achieved.

articleTitle: Research on the convolutional PML absorbing boundary conditions for the FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: The convolutional perfectly match layer (CPML) is a kind of widely-used absorbing boundary conditions (ABCs) for the finite-difference time domain (FDTD) method, but its complexity and intricacy makes it very difficult to be coded. Some easy-made mistakes such as incorrectly dealing with edges and angular points of CPML media, wrongly determining the coefficients of convolutional terms, etc., are introduced. In addition, a modified formula about CPML is proposed, which can improve its absorption performance greatly. A numerical experiment is presented to illustrate how to code the program correctly, Meanwhile, the calculation results show that the modified formula is more accurate in comparison with the conventional one.

articleTitle: Analysis of spread spectrum sliding correlator channel sounding under subway tunnel environment
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: To measure the time delay of signal propagation in underground environment of the subway tunnel, this paper adopted spread spectrum sliding correlation channel sounding methods. The paper describes the spread spectrum sliding correlation channel sounding principle in detail. According to the simulation, the method proposed can be used to measure the time delay of the channel of the subway tunnel.

articleTitle: Cellular automata self-organization algorithm for Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A WSN tends to be autonomic, an adaptive and distributive algorithm in Wireless Sensor Network is presented based on cellular automata mechanism, which was sourced from the thoughts of automatic breeding in biology. Each node of the Wireless Sensor Network is assumed to be equipped with CA machine, and change its state (active/stand-by) depends on the state of its neighbors. The main objective of this work is improving the transition function in the algorithm to guarantee the connectivity degree between nodes and network coverage with energy conservation. Simulation results demonstrate that the network has better properties under the condition of intensive node distribution, with the improved algorithm.

articleTitle: Circular polarization microstrip antenna array with compact structure for anticollision radar
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A multilayer slot-coupled microstrip antenna array is proposed for anticollision radar at 24GHz with circular polarization (CP) characteristic. The array is composed of 24 elements with 24-way microstrip line power divider network. The antenna can achieve CP by rotate the radiation patch a certain angle without polarizer. The VSWR coefficient of the array's ports is less than 1.8, and the side lobe level of array is below −26.5dB with axial ratio <3dB in the mainlobe beamwidth. This antenna array has compact structure and small size, thus it will not impair the automobile outline.

articleTitle: Research on a 0°∼360° FET analog phase shifter of x-band
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, the design of the 0°∼360° FET analog phase shifter is presented. By changing the gate voltages of the FET transistors, the output amplitudes of the four orthometric vector signals of the phase shifter can be independently adjusted. In this way, any phase shift over the range of 0° to 360° can be achieved. Due to the amplification characteristic of the FET transistors, the designed phase shifter has a gain rather than insertion loss. The gate voltages of the FETs are controlled by a microcontroller. Within the bandwidth of 400MHz (9.8GHz∼10.2GHz), the designed and fabricated 0°∼360° phase shifter's input and output VSWRs are less than 2∶1, the phase error is less then ±3°, and the in-band gain is about 7±0.5dB.

articleTitle: A channel popularity oriented transmission scheme in vehicular IPTV networks
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: IPTV services in vehicular networks are currently attracting increasingly more attentions. One essential challenge is to efficiently utilize the limited radio resources in vehicular access networks. This paper assumes that scalable video coding (SVC) is used to encode TV channels. Since TV channels usually possess different popularities, the paper proposes a novel transmission scheme, which employs differentiated modulation and coding scheme (MCS) profiles for channels of different popularities. The principle is to use more robust MCS profiles for more popular channels while to adopt higher efficient MCS profiles for less popular channels. Comparative simulation experiments are conducted and show that the proposed scheme can effectively and efficiently improve the gross channel availability (GCA) up to 10% compared to the baseline method.

articleTitle: Simulation of Electromagnetic Wave LWD tool response based on a volume integral equation method
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: An efficient volume integral equation (VIE) method based on piecewise constant basis functions (PWCBF) is presented for simulation of Electromagnetic Wave Logging-While-Drilling (EM LWD) tool response. The use of the basis allows a geometric discretization of nonconformal meshes, which leads to much flexibility in geometric modeling, but a hypersingular integral involving in the gradient-gradient operator applied on the Green's function must be handled. Examples of applying the VIE into modeling of EM LWD tool response are presented, which show the accuracy and efficiency of the scheme. An analytical method based on spherical functions expansion is used to obtain the exact electric fields radiated from transmitter coil of LWD tool in comparison with magnetic dipole approximation.

articleTitle: Design of the Hilbert fractal defected ground structure low-pass filter
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: The conventional micro-strip low-pass filter has the shortages of large size, narrow stop-band and wide transition band. To solve these problems, the Hilbert fractal defected ground structure (DGS) micro-strip low-pass filter is designed in this paper. The filter is cascaded by the Hilbert fractal DGS units and shunt branches. The Hilbert fractal DGS unit has a smaller size and can reduce the pass-band reflection loss, and the shunt branch can restrain the higher order harmonic components effectively so the stop-band performance is improved greatly. The tested results show that the cut-off frequency is up to 4.5GHz, the insert loss is less than 0.5dB at the pass-band, and the VSWR is less than 1.5 at the frequency range of 4GHz below. The stop-band suppression is less than -20dB from 5.5GHz to 14GHz, the reduction is more than 10dB, and the filter size is 24.4mm 7.43mm. The goals of miniaturization, high selectivity and wide stop-band low pass filter have been achieved.

articleTitle: Design of compact dual-mode dual-band filter based on frequency transformation method
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, a novel dual-mode resonator is presented, which is a square loop resonator attached by four arrow-shaped patches at the corners. By adding four patches and a perturbation to the square loop resonator, the features of compact size and controllable coupling are obtained. Coupling coefficient of the low modes and that of the high modes can be controlled independently when the dual-mode resonators cascade. Based on the resonator, a dual-band filter is designed using frequency transformation method. The building block is realized by a dual-mode resonator in stead of two common resonators. Due to the decrease in the number of resonators, the size of the designed filter can be reduced by half. A practical filter is fabricated and the measured results show good agreement with the design requirement.

articleTitle: A 610GHz imager In 0.18 micron CMOS process
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, a 610GHz imager composed of an on-chip antenna, a NMOS direct detector and an operational amplifier in 0.18 micron standard CMOS process is proposed. To satisfy the requirements of process design rules, we make some modifications to a rectangle patch antenna without lowering its performance. Based on the principle of distributed resistive self-mixing, the detector can work beyond the cutoff frequency of the technology and facilitate broadband detection. The operational amplifier makes use of a current mirror circuit to change a differential amplifier into a single-input-single-output circuit, which not only reduces common mode noise but matches the single-end antenna. According to our simulation, the imager achieves a responsivity (Rv) of 17.6 KV/W.

articleTitle: Complex infomax for blind separation of delayed sources
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: The information maximization (Infomax) based on information entropy theory is a class of methods that can be used to blindly separate mixed signals. In independent component analysis (ICA), the Infomax criterion is proposed by Bell and Sejnowski. Torkkola applied this criterion to separate the delayed sources blindly, which is more approximate to the real world than ICA model. However, Torkkola's method works only in the real-valued field. In this paper, we extend the Infomax for blind separation of delayed sources to the complex case and derive the adaptation rules based on gradient ascent. The simulation results illustrate the performance of the studied algorithm.

articleTitle: Add-select-delay-compare Viterbi decoder for UWB communications in electronic power systems
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In ultra-wideband (UWB) communications for power electronic systems, large power consumption and logic resource are occupied by multi-parallel sliding-block Viterbi decoders. A novel add-select-delay-compare architecture for Viterbi decoder is proposed to minimize these consumptions. In this architecture, a nested iteration of add-select and compare-select with balanced settling path is utilized to reduce propagation delay of critical path of add-compare-select and lower down parallel degrees of high throughput rate VD. The 500 Mbps UWB prototype receiver with the proposed add-select-delay-compare VD saves 40.4 % logic resource and 11.2 % power consumption compared with the original receiver.

articleTitle: The percolation process via a sinusoidal probability modulation
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: How clusters are aggregated have great effect on the function and dynamic of complex network. In this paper, we introduce a percolation transition model which can be described with clusters aggregated probability P(C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>) ∼ sin(αC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>/C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>), where C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> is the size of the cluster, C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> is the size of the largest cluster and α is disturbance parameter. In this article we introduce continuous, weakly and strongly discontinuous percolation transition underlying different α respectively and reveal the strongly impact of clusters' aggregated probability. By means of numerical simulation, we find that the critical point t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> shows periodic variation with increasing α. Besides, we realize that the largest gap is macroscopic when α >10.9π and the distribution of the cluster size at critical point meets the power laws which is the main feature of explosive percolation.

articleTitle: A four-way FDM intermediate frequency module for E-band communication applications
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper describes a four-path wideband intermediate frequency (IF) module with transceiver (TRX) functions for E-band application. To realize high capacity, the bandwidth of the IF module should be chosen considerately. The proposed IF module consists of four paths, which are combined by a combiner in the transmitter channel or separated by a splitter in the receiver channel, respectively. For each path, it includes an amplifier stage, a mixer stage and a variable-gain stage, as well as two filter stages. After the IF module is depicted, fabricated and measured, its dynamic ranges for both receiving and transmitting path are 31.5 dB, and its predicted noise figure (NF) of receiving path, including frontend, is 4.29dB. It is shown that the design IF module is suitable for E-band application.

articleTitle: A novel reflector antenna system generating orbital angular momentum
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A novel reflector antenna system generating electromagnetic field with orbital angular momentum (OAM) is proposed. Composed of a monofilar conical-helix antenna and a 20-cm-diameter parabolic-reflector, the proposed antenna system can radiate electromagnetic field with OAM of order 2. The simulated results along with some key parameters are presented and discussed in this study.

articleTitle: A novel PDF/PMF function based frequency allocation scheme in FFR aided OFDMA networks
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A novel frequency allocation scheme based on PDF/PMF functions of random variables is proposed in this paper, which is capable of adjusting the balance between long term fairness and performance in Fractional Frequency Reuse (FFR) aided Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access (OFDMA) networks. By adjusting the parameters of PDF/PMF functions the presented scheme achieves a flexible adjustment between user-fairness and cell-throughput. Simulation results indicate that compared to the Proportional Fairness (PF) allocation and equal rate allocation (ERA), the proposed scheme has significant performance advantage when the values of parameters are appropriate, and also has continuous controllability between ERA and maximum rate allocation (MRA).

articleTitle: A 300 GHz planar balanced quadrupler
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A 300 GHz quadrupler has been developed use AS1 Schottky diode. The quadrupler use the balanced planar diode configuration. The diode n-layer and n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-layer conductivity are given by GaAs semiconductor doping theory. Rs is given combined low-frequency simulation with empirical formula. The linear region is simulated in the HFSS, the S-parameter is imported into in the ADS. The quadrupler exhibits that the highest simulated efficiency is 7% at 306 GHz and the typical efficiency is 3% from 300 GHz to 308GHz.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of Sidelobe Canceller under the influence of ground clutter
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: By adopting Sidelobe Canceller (SLC) technology to realize spatial adaptive filtering in radar, it can eliminate the jamming from the antenna sidelobe. However, radar suffers serious ground clutter when detecting the target in low-altitude. The spatial complexity of ground clutter reduces the performance of SLC and even makes it invalid. Due to the influence of ground clutter, the optimum weighs calculated by SLC cannot be applied and the disagreement of main and auxiliary channel responses increases, which is certified by numerous simulation results in the case of standoff jamming and ground clutter. Therefore the estimate for the angle of arrival (AOA) of the jamming deviates from the real value. Besides, the bias of the AOA of the jamming increases against the jamming to clutter ratio (JCR) and the performance of SLC decreases consequently.

articleTitle: A low cost K-band FMCW radar system for automobile application
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, a low cost and compact K-band radar front-end, which can output FMCW signals in 23.76~24GHz with phase noise about -80dBc/Hz@10KHz and spurious suppression higher than 60dBc is designed. The frequency source part achieves the purposes of low power consumption and miniaturization with 2.8W DC power consumption and 58×53×19mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> dimension. The results of close loop experiments (3m, 4m, 5m, 7m, 8m, 9m) indicate the system can realize the function of measuring distance, and the measurement accuracy reaches the design goal.

articleTitle: Feasibility exploration of off-site TT&C Compatibility Test
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Through analyze the existing TT&C compatibility test, for the problem of long period and inefficiency, an off-site compatibility test method is proposed. This method installs the off-site compatibility test equipment in both ends of transponder and ground station which are apart. By building the system construction, the model of transmission link is drawn. In addition, based on the jitter of clock signal described in frequency, phase and time domain, the effect of jitter on signal coherence is deduced. It is shown that, the signal coherence won't be affected when using time and frequency remote calibration and traceability technology and system clocks which have good performance of short term frequency stability. In other words, the off-site TT&C compatibility test is feasibly.

articleTitle: The investigation of arm width in terahertz cross metal structures
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, the effects of the arm length and the width of cross-dipole and Jerusalem cross on resonance characteristics are investigated. By adjusting the geometry parameters of the two kinds of cross structures, the influence of arm length and width on the equivalent inductance and equivalent capacitance is analyzed by the simulations. The comparative analysis demonstrates that the width of cross-dipole has more influence on the equivalent inductance than equivalent capacitance. The conclusions in this paper would useful in the calculation of the equivalent inductance and capacitance in the LC resonance.

articleTitle: The study on the dualband filter with common cavity
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper introduces a method on the dualband filter with common cavity, which is based on the coupling matrix of the General Chebyshev filter, and then writing a matlab program can help us to get the parameters that we need more easier. In this article, the transmission band of the dualband filter is independently controlled. It can respectively by means of adjusting the coupling coefficients between the common cavity and the resonant units of the first passband filter and the second passband filter. At the same time, cross coupling is introduced in the passband filter, which is a good way to reduce the filter size. To verify the paper work, a dualband filter with common cavity design is introduced in the paper, whose test results and simulation results are perfectly identical with each other.

articleTitle: A simple ultra-wideband antenna with two frequency rejection bands
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: This paper presents a simple ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna with two frequency rejection bands. The two frequency rejection bands are obtained by using a pair of parallel coupling lines (PCL) and a loaded arc-shaped stub (ASS). The parallel coupling lines are inserted into the circular ring radiation patch, which is to produce the lower notch band at 3.5 GHz WiMAX band, while the loaded arc-shaped stub is connected to the coplanar waveguide (CPW) ground plane which is designed to give a higher notch at 5.5GHz WLAN band. Simulated results demonstrated that the proposed antenna can not only cover the entire UWB communication band but also have dual frequency rejection bands, which is suitable for indoor UWB communication applications.

articleTitle: Analysis and design of wideband bandpass filters with improved upper stopband
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Two high-order wideband bandpass filters with improved upper stopband based on transversal signal-interference techniques are analyzed and designed in this paper. By choosing different open stubs and open/shorted coupled lines, two wideband bandpass filters with several transmission zeros from 0 GHz to 2f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is center frequency of the stopband) can be achieved respectively, due to the superposition of signals of the two transmission paths. The bandwidths of the two wideband bandpass filters can be easily adjusted by changing the characteristic impedance of the resonant structures of the two transmission paths. One wideband bandpass filter prototype with 3-dB fractional bandwidth of 80% (0.6–1.8 GHz) is designed and fabricated for demonstration. The theoretical and measured results are in good agreement and show good in-band filtering performance and high selectivity.

articleTitle: OFDM -CPM performance analysis on Non-Continuous Wideband
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: OFDM-CPM is now a recognized alternative to conventional OFDM for the transmission of signals over Non-Continuous Wideband channel. This paper presents a characterization of nonlinear distortion effects in orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing/continuous phase modulation (OFDM-CPM) transmission systems on Non-Continuous Wideband. In a second step, a comparison with simulation results is carried out to show that OFDM-CPM is more suitable to attain high spectrum efficiency than OFDM-QPSK.

articleTitle: A novel LKH key tree structure based on heuristic search algorithm
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In multicast communication based on LKH, when a group member is added or evicted from the communication group, the system needs to update the group key to ensure the security of communication. In order to further reduce the rekey overhead, LKH is modified into a new key tree structure, which is constructed by heuristic search algorithm based on the number of group members. Compared to the LKH key tree structure, the branching factor of the new one can take on different value at each level. The experimental results showed the scheme proposed could efficiently reduce the encryption overhead, transmission overhead and the storage of keys during the rekey process.

articleTitle: Low complexity iterative equalizer for MIL-STD-188-110B appendix c
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Inter-symbol interference(ISI) makes a bad effect for communication system, which will increase the bit-error-rate(BER). In this paper, Three iterative equalizers are firstly compared, include the minimum mean-square error (MMSE), the MMSE with decision feedback (MMSE-DFE) and the soft-feedback interference cancellation (SFIC) equalizer. To trade-off BER performance and complexity of three iterative equalizers, a low complexity hybrid iterative equalizer is proposed to improve performance in mitigating inter-symbol interference over high frequency(HF) which uses MMSE-DFE for the first iterative and uses SFIC the rest. Despite the low complexity, the proposed scheme achieves better performance than the conventional MMSE-DFE for 3.5dB.

articleTitle: A CCM-based Pair-matching Method for Two-dimensional Arrival Angles Estimation
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
