abstract: This paper focuses on the pair-matching problem of Two-Dimensional Angle-Of-Arrival (2-D AOA) estimation for the L-shaped array. The authors adopt a modified array configuration in which the azimuth and elevation angles can be exploited independently. Moreover, by such configuration, the Cross Correlation Matrix (CCM) is employed to accomplish pairing-matching between estimated parameters which obtained by a subspace approach. Numerical simulations verify the effectiveness and performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of compact tri-band filter based on SIR-loaded resonator with 0° feed
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, a novel compact tri-band filter based on SIR loaded is presented. By adding λ/4 resonators and loading SIR stub, the features of compact size and tri-band response are obtained. Three passbands are designed to operate at 1.85GHz, 2.575GHz and 3.05GHz, respectively. The first and second passbands are obtained using resonator loaded with SIR, which is smaller in size than UIR, the λ/4 resonators is used to generate the third passband. The three passbands can be adjusted to designed values. The skew-symmetric (0-degree) feed structure was used to get a pair of transmission zeros so the frequency selectivity was greatly improved. Due to λ /4 resonators embedded in the resonator loaded with SIR, compact size for filter can be realized. A practical filter is fabricated and the measured results show good agreement with the design requirement.

articleTitle: Design of cross-coupling ceramic SIR narrowband filter
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, a microstrip bandpass filter based on cross-coupled is designed. Ceramic substrate with high dielectric constant and SIR structure are adopted. Because of Quarter-Wave and ceramic substrate, the whole size of the filter can be fabricated very small. Specifically, when the center frequency is 3.5GHz, its volume is 7mm*6.2mm*0.127mm. Besides the compact size, wide stopband and narrow passband makes it an excellent frequency-selecting filter.

articleTitle: Accurate rational model extraction method for lossy filter based on modified Cauchy method
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A lossy filter rational model extraction technique based on modified Cauchy method is presented in this paper. The conventional Cauchy method is only for lossless case, not suitable for lossy filter. The rational polynomials model is the prerequisite to synthesize the low-pass prototype (the evaluation of the coupling matrix) for computer-aided tuning. To this purpose, we modify the conventional Cauchy method to extract the accurate rational model of lossy filters. Three numerical examples verify the new technique successfully.

articleTitle: W band power amplifier based on 1 µm InP DHBT
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, a W-band power amplifier (PA) is presented by using 1 μm emitter length InP/InGaAs DHBT technology. The PA is consisted by 2 stages cascode cells and a common-emitter cell. The total circuit achieves more than 14 dB associate gain from 90 GHz to 98 GHz with input return loss greater than 30 dB and output return loss greater than 7 dB. The saturation output power reaches 18.5 dBm at 94 GHz. The chip area is 1.5 mm×1.1 mm.

articleTitle: A novel dual-polarized dielectric resonator antenna for 3.5 GHz LTE base station
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A novel dual-polarized dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) for 3.5 GHz LTE base station is presented in this paper. In the design, a hybrid feeding technique is used to obtain high-isolation and low cross-polarization. The bandwidths of both ports are increased by digging a symmetric hole in the dielectric resonator (DR). In addition, the symmetric radiation patterns could be obtained because of the strictly symmetric configuration of the antenna. Simulated result demonstrates that, the impedance bandwidths (VSWR <; 1.5) for port 1 and port 2 are 10% (3.31-4.62GHz) and 14% (3.35-3.85 GHz), respectively. High isolation (>34dB) and low cross-polarization level (>30dB) are also achieved over the entire operating bandwidth. The antenna has symmetric radiation patterns and 90 ± 5° half-power beamwidths in both ports.

articleTitle: Tolerance analysis of W-band SIW slot array antenna
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Tolerance analysis has been carried out for a 4 by 4 SIW slot array antenna in this paper. Variations of single geometrical parameter and multiple geometrical parameters have been used in the analysis with the help of full-wave electromagnetic simulator HFSS. The simulated results show that the PCB process is reliable for W-band SIW slot array antenna fabrication.

articleTitle: A comparative study of three transmission line models for on-chip interconnects
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, three effective transmission line (T-line) models are studied. One is the conventional frequency-dependent RLGC transmission line model which can think about the effect of skin effect and the dielectric-loss due to dielectric polarization and dipole rotation. The second is the fraction-order RLGC transmission line model which also considers the loss from frequency-dependent dispersion and non-quasi-static effects at Terahertz (THz) frequency band. Finally the third is the memory-dependent RLGC transmission line model through transfer function analysis, by comparing the poles and zeros of the transfer function of the equivalent circuit of the RLGC model, most of the parasitic effect including memory effect in THz frequency can be take into account. Three models are compared for on-chip coplanar waveguide (CPW) transmission lines over a wide frequency range from dc up to 67 GHz in SMIC 65 nm technology. And the memory-dependent model is much accurate than others.

articleTitle: Design of an X-band ridge-loaded staggered single-slot rectangular coupled-cavity traveling-wave tube
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: The paper describes the design of an X-band coupled-cavity traveling-wave tube (CC-TWT) based on the ridge-loaded staggered single-slot rectangular coupled-cavity slow wave structure (SWS) using High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) and particle-in-cell (PIC) code in Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Particle Studio. The working frequency range is from 8.6 to 9.5 GHz. The ridge can concentrate the longitudinal electric field in the structure so that the CC-TWT can produce 29.6 kW of saturated output power at 9 GHz with an electronic efficiency of 22.3 percent and a gain of 44.7 dB when the beam voltage is set to 26.9 kV and the beam current is set to 5 A.

articleTitle: Design of pulse-radiating bow-tie antenna with ellipsoid reflector for cancer treatment
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: A pulse-radiating bow-tie antenna with enhanced electric-field focusing property in the near field is studied. The focusing property is achieved by placing an ellipsoid reflector around the bow-tie antenna. A section of microstrip reflection line combined with a photoconductive semiconductor switches is designed as a source to generate a short pulse for antenna excitation. In simulations, the surrounding circumstance between the bow-tie antenna and the ellipsoid reflector is modeled as water to match with the real cellular environment. Results show that the electric field intensities of the proposed parabolic reflector antenna at 16 cm and 31cm from the radiating antenna are 1.5 v/m and 0.8 v/m, respectively, which is several times higher than that without the reflector. This merit makes the proposed antenna more suitable for cancer treatment.

articleTitle: Target detection technology based on quantitative analysis feature
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: Broadband high-resolution radar target echo is irradiated with multiple scattering centers. Echo distribute on each target range cell expansion. Signal is weak and decentralized energy distribution more, The noise power and the distribution of each unit are essentially the same distance. This makes the unit at the same distance, lower SNR, the effective signal detection becoming more difficult. Therefore, we must find ways to distinguish between useful signal and noise characteristics. By feature selection to find more efficient, lower dimension, more direct quality characteristics distinguishing the signal and noise. Therefore, feature extraction and feature selection are the most important issue facing the wideband radar signal detection and feature extraction. Selection is the key link which directly affects the performance of the merits of the broadband signal detection.

articleTitle: Four-band-notched UWB antenna using three circular split-rings and a square split-ring
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, a new design of a compact ultra-wideband monopole antenna covering 3.1-12 GHz with four band-notched characteristics is presented. The proposed antenna utilized three circular split-ring and a square split-ring to create four electromagnetic interference notched-bands including WLAN(5.15-5.35 GHz and 5.725-5.825 GHz), C-band(3.7-4.2 GHz) and X-band(7.3-7.8 GHz) satellite communication system and. Simulated results show that the designed antenna with compact size of 26×30 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> has an impedance of 3.1-12 GHz for VSWR less than 2 except the four frequency stop-bands to the UWB communication system. The results show that proposed antenna are very suitable for various portable UWB system.

articleTitle: Magnetic and substrate coupling effect between inductors in RFICs
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: The characterization on coupling effect of on-chip octagon spiral inductors has been presented. The coupling effects in different parted distances are presented. And the relationship between the coupling and the distance is plotted and discussed. What's more, a practical design tip about the distance of adjacent inductors is presented. Finally, the predominant role of coupling effect is investigated and discussed. And the magnetic coupling is the mainly consideration in applications below 7GHz.

articleTitle: Performance of RoFSO system with spatial diversity reception technology in strong atmospheric turbulence channel
publicationTitle: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Communiction Problem-solving
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the performance of radio over free space optical communication (RoFSO) system with spatial diversity reception technology (SDRT) operating over the gamma-gamma (GG) atmospheric turbulence channel. The bit error rate (BER) and outage probability of the system have been derived in closed form expressions using the generalized power series. For the same aperture size of the detectors, the SDRT can significantly improve the BER performance and outage probability of the RoFSO system. For example, the BER and the outage probability will decrease from ∼6.6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup> to ∼2.4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup> and from ∼2.3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup> to ∼4.9×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup> for using an extra photodetector (PD) at SNR=30dB in strong atmospheric turbulence regime.
